note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Sticky tokens: definition, detection, prevalence, impact and cause

nodes.name: Anomalous tokens alter similarity
nodes.description: Repeatedly inserting certain tokens into sentences changes text-embedding sentence similarity, e.g. appending 'lucrarea' to an unrelated sentence raises its Sentence-T5 similarity to a reference sentence.

nodes.name: Tokens pull similarity toward the mean
nodes.description: Anomalous tokens primarily pull pairwise sentence similarity toward the mean pairwise similarity of the model's token embeddings (about 0.8 for ST5-base), rather than always increasing it; normal tokens like 'and' have a much smaller impact.

nodes.name: Formal sticky token definition
nodes.description: A token t is sticky if, for all sentence pairs and all insertion operations (prefix, suffix, random) with n insertions, inserting t brings the pair's similarity within a threshold epsilon of the mean token similarity u.

nodes.name: STD detection pipeline
nodes.description: The Sticky Token Detector filters sentence pairs to those with similarity below u, removes undecodable and unreachable tokens, shortlists the top 2% of tokens by sticky score on sampled pairs, then validates shortlisted tokens against the definition on all filtered pairs with an adaptive threshold.

nodes.name: Sticky score
nodes.description: The sticky score combines the total positive and negative similarity changes, their frequencies, and the token's similarity to the sentence; hyperparameters chosen by ablation are n=8 insertions and k=5 sampled pairs.

nodes.name: 868 sticky tokens found
nodes.description: STD finds 868 sticky tokens across 40 checkpoints of 12 text-embedding model families evaluated on MTEB STS datasets; sticky tokens make up 0.4% to 5.3% of shortlisted candidates, or 0.006% to 1% of vocabulary.

nodes.name: Origins: special and unused tokens
nodes.description: About 7% (64) of sticky tokens are special/control tokens ([CLS], [SEP], [MASK], [PAD], </s>) and unused tokens like <extra_id_27> frequently appear, e.g. </s> appears in 12 T5-based checkpoints.

nodes.name: Origins: multilingual fragments
nodes.description: About 22% (191) of sticky tokens contain non-English characters such as Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic and combining/math symbols, suggesting limited non-English coverage in pre-training.

nodes.name: Prevalence not tied to scale
nodes.description: Sticky token counts do not consistently correlate with model or vocabulary size (Spearman rho=0.127, p=0.706 for T5 models; sentence-t5-xl has 34 but xxl 22; gte-Qwen2-7B has 103 while GritLM-7B has 17), and models in the same family often share sticky tokens.

nodes.name: Sticky tokens degrade downstream tasks
nodes.description: Inserting sticky tokens degrades MTEB clustering and retrieval much more than normal tokens (paired t-test, p=0.017, Cohen's d=0.41); for ST5-base SciFact falls 41.5% (45.76 to 26.76) and NFCorpus 52.3%, versus about 2.6% and 0.56% for normal tokens.

nodes.name: Robustness varies with model
nodes.description: Lightweight models degrade catastrophically (sentence-t5-base Biorxiv clustering 23.11 to 15.02, -35.0%) while larger models like UAE-Large-V1 stay robust (SciFact 73.91 to 72.63, -1.7%).

nodes.name: Sticky tokens dominate attention
nodes.description: In ST5-base, attention weights on appended sticky tokens concentrate in high-value ranges (>0.4) in intermediate layers, whereas normal tokens have a smoother Gaussian-like distribution.

nodes.name: Anomalies amplify across layers
nodes.description: The Wasserstein distance between sticky and normal token attention patterns is moderate in early layers (1-6), grows in mid-to-late layers (6-12) and peaks at the final layers, so small irregularities are progressively amplified.

isolated_nodes.name: Limitation: scope of detection
isolated_nodes.description: Detection covers open-source, mostly BPE-based text embedding models; closed-source or Unigram-tokenizer models may differ, and non-isotropic embedding spaces may need tailored criteria.

isolated_nodes.name: No mitigation proposed
isolated_nodes.description: The paper does not propose concrete mitigations such as tokenizer retraining or embedding-space regularization.

isolated_nodes.name: All 40 models anisotropic
isolated_nodes.description: All 40 evaluated embedding models exhibit anisotropic behavior.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from observation of anomalous tokens, to the formal definition and detector, to prevalence findings, downstream damage, and attention-based explanation.
